title: LLM Evaluation Frameworks (TruLens/Ragas)
summary: Evaluate agent and RAG behavior with versioned datasets, component metrics, calibrated judges, and release criteria tied to actual task outcomes.
overview: Evaluation frameworks organize datasets, execution traces, scoring, and comparisons across application versions. TruLens and Ragas provide useful evaluation capabilities, but the architecture must still define what success means for the product. A metric is a measurement instrument with assumptions, not an automatic release decision.

For RAG, distinguish retrieval relevance, answer relevance, and support by retrieved evidence. Faithfulness to a retrieved passage does not prove that the passage is true or current. For agents, add tool selection, argument correctness, authorization, side-effect outcomes, and completion criteria. Evaluate the trajectory when the final answer hides an unsafe or wasteful path.

production.poc: A prototype needs a small representative set with reviewed expected behavior. Include unanswerable questions and tool failures, not only successful demonstrations.
production.production: Production versions datasets, prompts, models, judge configurations, and scoring code. Calibrate model judges against human labels and retain uncertainty rather than treating every score as exact.
production.scale: At scale, combine offline release tests with sampled production evaluation. Segment results by tenant, language, intent, and risk so aggregate improvements cannot hide critical regressions.

components.name: Evaluation dataset
components.role: Contains representative inputs, expected behavior, evidence, and meaningful failure cases.

components.name: Execution recorder
components.role: Captures retrieval, tool calls, model versions, and outcomes with appropriate data minimization.

components.name: Metric pipeline
components.role: Computes deterministic checks and model-assisted scores for distinct quality dimensions.

components.name: Human calibration set
components.role: Establishes agreement and failure modes of automated judges.

components.name: Release gate
components.role: Applies risk-weighted thresholds and compares candidates with a versioned baseline.

flow.title: Define quality
flow.description: Translate product requirements into observable success and failure criteria.

flow.title: Build cases
flow.description: Sample realistic workloads and add adversarial, missing-evidence, and degraded-dependency examples.

flow.title: Run candidates
flow.description: Execute identical cases with pinned application and data versions where feasible.

flow.title: Score dimensions
flow.description: Separate retrieval, grounding, task completion, safety, latency, and cost measurements.

flow.title: Calibrate judgments
flow.description: Review disagreements and estimate uncertainty for model-based metrics.

flow.title: Decide and monitor
flow.description: Apply release criteria, preserve evidence, and compare production drift against the baseline.

useCase.title: Evaluating a technical support assistant
useCase.situation: A software vendor updates retrieval and prompts for an assistant that diagnoses integration errors.
useCase.problem: A higher average answer score can conceal incorrect tool arguments and regressions on rare authentication failures.
useCase.requirement: The assistant must resolve supported cases with correct evidence and safe tool usage under practical latency and cost limits.
useCase.architecture: A versioned evaluation suite combines RAG metrics, deterministic tool-contract checks, and analyst-labeled resolution outcomes.
runtime: The candidate runs against the same support cases and source snapshot as the current release.
Reviewers inspect judge disagreements and high-impact regressions before a release decision is recorded.
useCase.failure: If the judge model changes, the team recalibrates scores rather than interpreting a shifted scale as product improvement.
useCase.impact: Track resolution quality, unsupported claims, tool accuracy, judge agreement, and cost per successful case. Framework scores are diagnostic signals, not universal quality guarantees.

tradeoffs.benefit: Semantic evaluation scales beyond exact string matching.
tradeoffs.cost: Bias, inconsistency, and correlated errors require calibration.

tradeoffs.benefit: More workload variation can be represented.
Important regressions are caught before deployment.
tradeoffs.cost: Noisy metrics can block useful changes without uncertainty handling.

failures.scenario: A candidate learns the test set's wording
failures.detection: Held-out and production cases show weaker performance.
failures.recovery: Refresh representative cases and preserve a protected evaluation split.

failures.scenario: Aggregate scores hide one critical intent regression
failures.recovery: Block release for that criterion and repair the affected path.

mistakes.fix: Check source authority and task correctness separately.
Pin or recalibrate the judge to preserve comparability.
Evaluate tools, evidence, permissions, and external effects.

whenToUse: Model or retrieval changes need evidence-based comparison.
Agent behavior has measurable task outcomes.
Release decisions require repeatable quality and risk signals.
whenNotToUse: A framework is being used without product-specific criteria.
No representative data or review capacity exists.
One aggregate score is expected to prove system safety.
checklist: Record release thresholds and uncertainty handling.
